purpose: Third-party JavaScript/TypeScript source files that the mutation generator (evaluation/generators) turns into evaluation cases. Every repository is pinned to a commit and every file to a SHA-256; nothing here is fetched at generation time.
threats: Contamination: these are popular public libraries and may be present in a language model's training data. A one-line mutant is new text, but the surrounding code may be memorized, which can flatter an AI arm.
Mutant realism: seeded edits are a proxy for real faults; equivalence is 'unchecked', so some mutants may not change behavior.
Rule alignment: the rule-aligned stratum inserts patterns Arm A's rules target, so it must be reported separately from the logic stratum.
Mutants are checked for syntax only (not types or tests): a mutant that a type checker or the project's tests would reject instantly still counts as a defect here.
